parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
A ball of mass 0.45 kg leaves the edge of a table with a horizontal velocity $v$, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}

The height of the table is 1.25 m. The ball travels a distance of 1.50 m horizontally before hitting the floor.

Air resistance is negligible.

Calculate, for the ball,
parts.text: the horizontal velocity v as it leaves the table, $v = \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the velocity just as it hits the floor,

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
the kinetic energy just as it hits the floor, $\text{kinetic energy} = J$

(J)

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
the loss in gravitational potential energy as it falls from the table to the floor.
loss in potential energy = J

(J)

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why the kinetic energy of the ball in (b)(iii) does not equal the loss of gravitational potential energy in (b)(iv).
